one_liner: SIMD b-ary Segment-Tree index for rank/select/flip on mutable bitmaps; paper reports it beats Marchini-Vigna compact Fenwick trees.
what_it_does: Header-based C++17 library that keeps rank, select, access and flip on a fixed-size bitmap all fast. You build an mrs::mutable_bitmap<SearchablePrefixSums<Height>, BlockType> from an array of 64-bit words, then call rank(i), select(i), access(i) and flip(i). It cannot grow or shrink: flip toggles bits in place, and there is no insert, delete or append. It is a research codebase with no packaged API, and the tree height is a compile-time template parameter that you work out from the bitmap size.
how_it_is_fast: The bitmap is split into 256- or 512-bit blocks. Per-block popcounts go into a b-ary Segment-Tree of searchable prefix sums with fanout 128 at the leaves, then 64, 64 and 32, so at most 4 levels cover 2^24 blocks. Each node stores 8-way segment summaries plus in-segment prefix sums, so a sum is two loads, a search is two SIMD compares (_mm256_cmpgt_epi32 plus a first-set scan), and an update is two SIMD adds of a precomputed +1/-1 table row. Within a block, rank uses unrolled or looped popcount and select uses popcount plus PDEP/TZCNT, with an optional AVX-512 VPOPCNTDQ path.
when_to_use: Bitmaps whose bits change often (flip-heavy workloads such as dynamic sets, deletion markers, or dynamic FM-index or wavelet-tree components) where you still need rank/select in tens of nanoseconds.
x86-64 servers with AVX2, ideally AVX-512 (VL, BW, VPOPCNTDQ), where the paper says the AVX-512 build roughly doubles search speed over AVX2.
Fixed-capacity bitmaps of up to 2^32 bits (256-bit blocks) or 2^33 bits (512-bit blocks), where about 3.6-7.2% extra space is acceptable.
Research or benchmarking of dynamic rank/select, since the repo also ships Marchini and Vigna's hybrid Fenwick trees (include/hft) and their benchmark driver (src/perf_hft.cpp).
when_not_to_use: Static bitmaps: an immutable rank/select directory (rank9/poppy-style, pasta, SPIDER, 3*) uses less space and needs no update path.
Bitmaps that must grow, shrink, or take inserts and deletes; only flip is supported, and the size is fixed at build.
Non-x86 targets: access() is x86 inline assembly (bt/sbb), and the SIMD paths need AVX2 or AVX-512 intrinsics. -DDISABLE_AVX swaps the SIMD node code for scalar loops, but the inline assembly stays.
Bitmaps larger than 2^24 blocks: build() rejects them only through assert, which compiles out in release builds.
Production code that needs a maintained, packaged dependency: last commit January 2023, no releases, no issues filed, and the README describes it as a research artifact for the paper.

integration.dependencies: essentials (jermp/essentials, used by segment_tree::bytes()); the tests and benchmarks also use doctest and cmd_line_parser. The top-level CMakeLists requires Boost (unit_test_framework, iostreams, system, filesystem), and its succinct and sdsl-lite submodules are only for the immutable-bitmap benchmark.
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (if constexpr, structured bindings); README tested gcc 7.4 and 9.2.1, clang 10.0.0 and 11.0.0; CMake 2.8+; builds with -march=native by default
integration.platforms: x86-64 only (inline bt/sbb asm in access(); AVX2 by default, AVX-512F/BW/VL/VPOPCNTDQ plus BMI2 with -DAVX512=On); tested on Linux and macOS 10.14
integration.thread_safety: not documented; queries are const members with no internal state, so concurrent reads look safe, but flip is unsynchronized
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: it covers the same operations as a Fenwick-tree mutable bitmap (rank, select, flip), but has its own API and compile-time Height parameter, and is not interchangeable with sux classes

gotchas: Height is a template parameter that must match the number of blocks (segment_tree::height(n) gives it). A mismatch is caught only by assert, and in release builds a too-small Height makes build() index num_nodes_per_level with a negative level, which is out-of-bounds.
select(i) only asserts i < size() (bits), not i < number of ones; asking for a select past the popcount is undefined in release builds.

Benchmark harness bug: src/perf_prefix_sum.cpp and src/perf_hft.cpp test operation == "sarch" (typo) when choosing search queries, so 'search' benchmarks draw targets from [0, n) instead of [0, total sum). Both the Segment-Tree and the Fenwick prefix-sum search timings therefore query only a small prefix of the sums. The bitmap-level benchmark (perf_mutable_bitmap select) draws queries correctly from [0, num_ones).
Headers are not self-contained (util.hpp has no includes; mutable_bitmap.hpp uses std::memcpy and std::ceil without <cstring>/<cmath>), so include order matters if you vendor them.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over static rank/select siblings (SPIDER, 3*-rankselect, rankselect/PTSelect, succinct-bitvec-cpp, QuadRank) when bits change after construction, which those do not support. Prefer them for read-only bitmaps, where they are smaller and need no update path.
verified_claims_summary: Search snippets of the Information Systems 2021 paper (the paper itself was not opened) say the SIMD b-ary Segment-Tree is consistently faster than Marchini and Vigna's compact Fenwick trees for rank, select and flip on random workloads, at 3.6-7.2% extra space, measured on an Intel i9-9940X at 3.30 GHz with -O3 -march=native. No ratio was seen. Contrary to the verifier's note, the repo does build the Fenwick competitor, but only at the prefix-sum level: src/perf_hft.cpp benchmarks the hft ByteF/BitF/FixedF/ByteL/BitL/FixedL classes against src/perf_prefix_sum.cpp, not at the full-bitmap level.
status_note: Abandoned since January 2023 (123 commits, no releases, no issues), but MIT-licensed and a small header set that can be vendored with essentials; x86-only.
